meta.name: HAX ecosystem
meta.about: Details for hax-ecosystem.mmd. Structure lives in the Mermaid file; this file holds descriptions, links, releases, evidence, tours and timeline years. Run scripts/graph-drift.mjs after each release to refresh versions and flag what changed.
pairs: haxcms-php and haxcms-nodejs ship together and should carry the same version.

human.desc: People are the center of HAX: authors, students, faculty, staff and contributors. Every pillar exists for them.

traveler.desc: The HAX mascot, the Future Traveler: "Dream it, remix it, have it, share it." Here he stands for your AI companion, working alongside people.

accessible.desc: Built for everyone, by everyone. Everything HAX makes meets accessibility standards by default, so authors don't need to be experts to publish work everyone can use. Blocks are tested for contrast, keyboard use and screen readers before they ship, and meaning never depends on color alone. HAX also reaches a global audience, with an interface in over 100 languages. And since you don't need to know what the web is to use it, anyone can contribute.

efficient.desc: Fast for the people who make it and the people who use it. Authors build sites in minutes, not weeks, and agents can handle the repetitive work. Pages load only what they need, so they're fast on any connection or device. The less time we spend waiting and trying to figure out how to use something, the more time we spend dreaming the future together.

extensible.desc: If it's missing, anyone can build it. Every block and theme in HAX is a web component, so new ones follow the same rules as the ones we ship. Plugins add choices and integrations without changing the core. And because HAX can understand any block's settings, anything you build works in the editor right away.

open.desc: Open by design: built on standards, owned by you. HAX is free, open source under Apache 2.0, and built on open standards like web components, OpenAPI, WCAG and xAPI instead of a proprietary framework. Your site is plain HTML files you can take anywhere, with no lock-in and no subscription. What you make is yours to keep, change, share or move, however you see fit.

agnostic.desc: Any format, any screen, any browser. Bring content in from Word, PDFs, old sites or other CMSs, and HAX turns it into clean web pages. Those pages work on phones, tablets, laptops and big screens, in light or dark mode. Run it on PHP, Node, the command line, the desktop app, or as a static site with no server at all.

remixable.desc: Break it down, mix it up, make it new. Every page is made of blocks you can rearrange, reuse or pull into another site. Bring in PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, HTML or Markdown, and export to PDF, EPUB and other open formats. Change the theme any time and your content comes along untouched, and anything an agent makes stays fully editable by a person.

sustainable.desc: Built to last, light on the planet. Nearly every site built since 2020 still works today, and new features reach old sites through upgrades, without rebuilds. Sites are small, load only what they need, and can run as static files, which saves energy on every visit. And the project is built to outlast any one person, with its knowledge recorded so the community can carry it forward.

haxcms.desc: "A hybrid static site generator, a new class of CMS": a microsite generator and manager that doesn't need the command line.
haxcms.yearNote: HAXcms announced at DrupalCon; the first site goes live

editor.desc: HAX, the Headless Authoring eXperience: "a WYSIWYG unlike any other. You extend your world by extending the web through the web component standard."
editor.yearNote: HAX first presented at DrupalCon Baltimore by Bryan Ollendyke and Michael Potter

merlin.desc: HAX's command program, marked by the wand: search for and run actions while editing. HAX Tips will surface here.

dashboard.desc: app-hax, where people create and manage sites. Three generations were built by student teams from 2022 to 2026.
dashboard.yearNote: Dashboard 1.0 built by a student team in one semester

themes.desc: Ways to theme HAXcms matched to skill set: skin a site with CSS, or build a theme from web components. Themes grew from 14 at the end of 2024 to more than 30.

php.desc: HAXcms on PHP. Kept in step with the Node.js backend through a shared OpenAPI contract; powers haxtheweb.org through HAXiam.

nodejs.desc: HAXcms on Node.js, started with npx @haxtheweb/haxcms-nodejs. The most-downloaded @haxtheweb package.

haxiam.desc: Makes HAXcms multi-tenant: hundreds of sites from one core behind institutional login. hax.psu.edu runs on it.
haxiam.yearNote: HAXiam: many HAXcms sites behind one login

haxpsu.desc: Penn State's HAXcms service, run on HAXiam behind Penn State login: 302 sites, 368 users and 17,100 pages. "Free, open source, forever, transformative, unleashing creativity in a sustainable way." Open its web for courses by college.

ssr.desc: Lit server-side rendering so elements render for search engines and AI crawlers. Publish-time static SSR comes first; serving SSR live is parked until it is stable.
ssr.yearNote: Server-side rendering for search engines and AI

hax11ty.desc: "HAX + 11ty = HAX11ty! The best of SEO from 11ty while using the HAX editor and the HAXcms theme engine."
hax11ty.yearNote: HAX11ty, made for the Libraries plays

cli.desc: hax: install with npm install --global @haxtheweb/create, then run hax start. Creates sites and components, audits DDD and publishes. Needs Node 20+.
cli.yearNote: Winston White builds much of the HAX CLI

ubiquity.desc: The webcomponents release build that ships every element, as one tested set, to haxcms-nodejs and the other backends.
ubiquity.yearNote: Ubiquity: one tested release build of every element

staticpub.desc: Static export and Lit SSR built into haxcms-nodejs, haxcms-php and the CLI, so any site publishes as static files from core; HAX11ty becomes a wrapper around it.

magiclink.desc: One-time login links issued from the CLI, so an admin can recover or hand out access without a password.

importers.desc: Every way content gets into HAX: whole sites from WordPress, Drupal, Plone, ELMS:LN, Notion, GitBook, VitePress, Quarto, Pressbooks, OpenStax or any HTML site; a site from one Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF or HTML file; and documents, media or links dropped into the page you are writing.
importers.yearNote: Importers: every way content gets into HAX

flows.desc: Three paths through HAX in order: how a page loads, how a page is added, and how a site is restructured with the outline designer. Open it and press Play.

learnhax.desc: Learn HAX: tutorials, reference and onboarding for the HAX ecosystem, at learn.haxtheweb.org. This web is meant to fold into it.

deploy.desc: Publish targets for HAX sites: surge, Netlify, Vercel and GitHub Pages, as static files.
deploy.yearNote: Publishing HAX sites to static hosts

ai.desc: AI features inside HAX: Dave Fusco's AI integration from the AI and HAX grant, and Zach Dodson's AI chat agent.

agents.desc: Agent skills for HAX, split between PRAW (community and administration) and create (using HAX). With PRAW's context, closed issues per month rose about 90%, then 211%.

mcp.desc: An MCP server so agents can work with HAXcms sites. It connects to the Node.js and PHP backends and the CLI; it is not enabled on HAXiam deployments.

praw.desc: "A repository containing comprehensive AI agent rules for the HAX ecosystem": the worldview, voice, wins and skills that keep agents and contributors consistent.

issues.desc: The unified HAX issue queue for every project, including published security advisories.

wins.desc: "Sourced stories that prove the worldview works." A good win has a person, a before and after, and a source.
wins.yearNote: WINS: sourced stories that prove the worldview works

haxcamp.desc: Gatherings to learn web components. The first, hosted by Duke, drew over 40 people.

components.desc: About 640 web components open sourced by May 2026; 289 @haxtheweb packages on npm, downloaded about 49,000 times a month. Open the Web components web to see the 60 blocks in the HAX app store.

ddd.desc: DDD (Design, Develop, Deliver), the HAX design system. It began as Keith Charlton Jr's class project and now spans 60+ elements: "PSU-esque designs by PSU."

source.label: WINS.md: Students built the design system

plugins.desc: A plugin architecture in progress: spec and examples in haxcms-plugin-examples, while core keeps the evolving baseline (SEO, accessibility, sitemaps).

languages.desc: Internationalization for any web component, plus a shared registry of 102 supported languages being built in phases.
languages.yearNote: Languages: i18n for any web component

insights.desc: A planned admin dashboard of stats computed from site content: content, broken links, accessibility and where to add activities.
insights.yearNote: Insights, What's New and Tips on the dashboard

presentations.desc: Talks, podcasts and webinars about HAX from 2017 to 2026. Open the Presentations web to see each one, who gave it, where and what it covered.
presentations.yearNote: The first HAX talk, at DrupalCon Baltimore

ist256.desc: Bryan's advanced web development course at Penn State: vanilla web components and Lit, ending in real contributions to HAX. Taught from fall 2019 to spring 2026; many class projects became HAX components. Open the IST 256 web for semesters and projects.

grants.desc: Faculty and unit grants that fund real student work on HAX. Grant sizes are left out on purpose: it isn't a competition, and this work doesn't need much money.

g_fusco.desc: Dave Fusco's grant for AI and HAX: Canvas AI analysis built by students through the HAX CLI, reporting how AI-ready a course's assignments are and launching a live HAX site.
g_fusco.yearNote: Dave Fusco's AI and HAX grant

g_frank.desc: Jennifer Frank's grant for the International Student Portfolio: Winston White's work on HAXcms and skeletons, so students get portfolios they can take with them.
g_frank.yearNote: Jennifer Frank's International Student Portfolio grant

g_hhd.desc: With Health and Human Development: Bryan, Bill and Blake Colaianne, for making more games and improving web components and HAXcms.
g_hhd.yearNote: HHD grant with Bill, Bryan and Blake

games.desc: Playful games and media built from HAX web components, like rpg-character games starring the Future Traveler.

buttercups.desc: Buttercups Training, a UK training company that contributed to ELMS:LN and the HAX editor from 2019 to 2022: HAX content hooks, a TinCan (xAPI) bridge fix, H5P updates and MOOC content.
buttercups.yearNote: Buttercups Training starts contributing to ELMS:LN

innovationhub.desc: The Eric J. Barron Innovation Hub, Penn State's coworking and collaboration space in downtown State College. Its earlier site was built on hax.psu.edu.

wcstandard.desc: The browser-native component model HAX is built on: "Web components effectively turn the HTML of a site into a consistent API."
wcstandard.yearNote: Mike Potter points Bryan to the web component standard

security.desc: 39 published advisories in the unified queue, many found by Penn State's CCSO students, who helped resolve 30 vulnerabilities over two years.
security.yearNote: CCSO's first audit; the first CVEs are published

testing.desc: Automated tests that check human- and AI-made changes: Chromium on every pull request, full cross-browser runs outside CI.

design.desc: The UX and visual design practice behind HAX UI and DDD, shaped by student UX groups and the 2019 National Archives usability audit.
design.yearNote: The design practice behind HAX UI and DDD

jos.desc: JSON Outline Schema: the site structure (site.json) HAXcms is built on, effectively one to one.
jos.yearNote: JSON Outline Schema becomes the site structure

haxschema.desc: "For your element to talk to the HAX editor, you implement static get haxProperties()": the schema that gives every block its editing form.
haxschema.yearNote: HAXSchema: elements describe themselves to the editor

appstore.desc: The app store spec: the autoloader "loads all the elements that will be available to your users", plus stax (templates) and blox (layouts).
appstore.yearNote: The app store spec: the editor loads only the elements a site needs

oerschema.desc: Metadata for open educational resources, kept with the content so it can be found, credited and remixed. Authored by Michael Collins.
oerschema.yearNote: OER Schema for open educational resources

openapi.desc: The shared contract that keeps haxcms-nodejs and haxcms-php input and output identical.
openapi.yearNote: One OpenAPI contract for haxcms-nodejs and haxcms-php

community.desc: How HAX is run: roles and succession, how a decision is made in the open, the documents every repo keeps, and where people meet.

quality.desc: Every safeguard on what enters HAX: blocking pull request gates, advisory checks, and nightly and weekly jobs, generated from the CI that actually runs.

heosat.desc: HEOSAT, Apereo's Higher Education Open Source Assessment Toolkit: 47 questions in 9 sections on licensing, governance, community, docs, operations, security, standards, adoption and sustainability. HAX runs it with AI through the heosat skill in PRAW, a process worked out with Apereo. Open it to see every question and what answers it.

booklooky.desc: BookLooky, a fellow open source project. HAX's AI-run HEOSAT process helped it go through Apereo incubation more accurately, and PRAW's haxcms-lrs-rater skill runs its Looky Rating System.

wcag.desc: WCAG, the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines from the W3C. HAX elements are built to meet them by default; element test suites run axe accessibility checks where an element has tests, and the weekly accessibility sweep checks every demo.

meaningchannels.desc: The meaning channels standard: anything that carries meaning or a consequential decision (correct versus incorrect, confirm versus deny, saving or deleting permanently) is conveyed through five channels at once: a label on hover and focus, a distinct color (green for correct, purple for incorrect, not red), a focus state, a texture that survives grayscale, and an icon unique to that meaning. Written into PRAW RULES.md; not yet in the DDD docs, and no gate enforces it yet.

sdgs.desc: The UN Sustainable Development Goals HAX meets: 4 Quality Education, 7 Affordable and Clean Energy, 8 Decent Work and Economic Growth, 9 Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure, 10 Reduced Inequalities, 12 Responsible Consumption and Production, 17 Partnerships for the Goals. The un-sdg element shows them on HAX pages; the docs tie 7 and 12 to the Efficient pillar.

rules.desc: Rules and guarantees: every rule HAX keeps, generated from PRAW's RULES.md and each repo's AGENTS.md, linked up to the pillars it serves, across to the parts it touches and down to the checks that enforce it. A rule nothing enforces shows as a gap.

contracts.desc: Every data contract in one view: the schema files each HAX format is defined by, and who reads and writes them.

anatomy.desc: What a HAX site is made of on disk: site.json, pages, files, theme, the registry and the files HAXcms generates.

xapi.desc: Learner activity recorded as xAPI-style statements, ready to move from local storage to a learning record store.

registry.desc: The manifests HAX generates about its own elements: wc-registry.json (where every tag loads from), each package's custom-elements.json, the elements catalog, and the language and translation manifests. tours.label: Everyone
tours.message: HAX in one pass: people at the center, the pillars they hold, and everything that connects to them.

scenes.caption: Humans are at the center of HAX.
People hold the seven pillars that make it powerful.
The Future Traveler is your AI companion, working alongside you.
It began at Penn State, with ELMS:LN and the people who built it.
Penn State backs the work through its colleges and University Libraries.
You build with HAXcms on PHP, Node.js, the CLI or HAX11ty.
Authoring happens in the editor, Merlin, themes and the dashboard; open HAXcms for every admin piece.
The building blocks rest on the web component standard.
Schemas are the contracts that keep every part portable.
Skeletons make courses, blogs, portfolios and department sites reusable.
HAX Lab and student clubs bring design and security; HAX Camp and DrupalCon grow the community.
Students and faculty built much of what you see.
The traveler learns from PRAW, skills, the MCP and the issue queue, checked by automated tests.
IST 256 turns students into contributors; grants fund the work.
Apereo, GitHub and npm connect HAX to the open source world; Buttercups Training contributed from the UK.
Ubiquity, Lit SSR and deploy targets ship it anywhere, fast.
WINS keeps the proof: the people and groups it helped.
One web of connections. Every part makes every other part stronger.

tours.label: Faculty
tours.message: Build a course, portfolio or department site yourself, keep it accessible by default, and own it for good.

scenes.caption: You are at the center, with the pillars that protect your work.
HAXcms and the editor: authoring without a web team or the command line.
Start from a skeleton for a course, portfolio, textbook or department site.
OER Schema and xAPI keep your content open and your learners' progress visible.
Faculty like you already build on it.
Penn State hosts it for you on hax.psu.edu.

tours.label: Students
tours.message: Learn modern front-end web by contributing to a real project. Your work ships, gets credited, and goes with you.

scenes.caption: It starts with people, including you.
HAX Lab, IST and the student clubs are the way in.
Web components, DDD and the CLI are what you'll learn and build.
Students built the dashboard, DDD, the CLI and skeletons.
CCSO students found and fixed real vulnerabilities, with CVEs to show for it.
Your contributions go on GitHub and npm, and into WINS.

tours.label: Developers
tours.message: Standards all the way down: web components, an OpenAPI contract, a CLI and agent tooling you can extend without forking.

scenes.caption: The web component standard is the foundation.
Components, DDD and HAXSchema make every block editable by people and machines.
Two backends, one OpenAPI contract, plus the CLI and HAX11ty.
The MCP (pre-release), PRAW and skills let agents work the same way.
Ubiquity, SSR, tests and deploy targets ship it.
Everything is on GitHub and npm, with one issue queue.

tours.label: Partners
tours.message: Free and open, backed by Penn State and the Apereo community, with sourced proof of what it does.

scenes.caption: People and the pillars come first.
Penn State backs HAX across its colleges and libraries.
Open source homes: Apereo, DrupalCon, GitHub and npm.
A pipeline of students keeps it moving, at Penn State and Georgia Tech.
WINS has the proof.
Proof outside the for-credit course: public training, open editions and a listening room.

tours.label: Administrators
tours.message: Host it your way: PHP or Node.js, many sites with HAXiam, static publishing, and a public security record.

scenes.caption: Pick a backend: PHP or Node.js, kept identical by OpenAPI.
HAXiam runs hundreds of sites from one core behind your login.
Security is audited in public, with student auditors and automated tests.
Publish static sites anywhere.
The MCP is pre-release and not enabled on HAXiam.

tours.label: Follow one piece of content
tours.message: What remixability means in practice: one page, from a person typing to a published, machine-readable site.

scenes.caption: A person writes a page in the HAX editor.
The page is saved as HTML in a site described by JSON Outline Schema, tagged with OER Schema.
HAXcms on PHP or Node.js stores and serves it, both keeping the same OpenAPI contract.
It leaves as a static publish or server-rendered for search engines and AI.

tours.label: Why we're sustainable
tours.message: For funders, administrators and leadership: institutional backing plus open infrastructure means the project lasts.

scenes.caption: Penn State backs HAX.
Five colleges and units teach and publish with it.
Students audit its security through CCSO.
The Apereo Foundation supports it beyond one university.
GitHub and npm carry it as open infrastructure.
WINS keeps the evidence.

tours.label: Your first contribution
tours.message: For students and new contributors: the path from coursework to real contributions.

scenes.caption: A class project in IST 256.
Becomes a HAX component.
PRAW and its agent skills show you the conventions.
The HAX CLI scaffolds, audits and ships it.

tours.label: Pick your pillar
tours.message: One short scene per pillar, for a talk that needs one focused angle.

scenes.caption: Accessible: Built for everyone, by everyone.
Efficient: Fast for the people who make it and the people who use it.
Extensible: If it's missing, anyone can build it.
Open: Open by design: built on standards, owned by you.
Agnostic: Any format, any screen, any browser.
Remixable: Break it down, mix it up, make it new.
Sustainable: Built to last, light on the planet.
All seven pillars, held by people.

tours.label: The AI companion
tours.message: HAX's AI-forward direction: humans and AI remixing each other's work in a standards-compliant, accessible way.

scenes.caption: A person.
Works alongside the Future Traveler.
Who learns the conventions from PRAW and its agent skills.
And reaches HAXcms through the MCP (pre-release), the same OpenAPI contract people use.
The HAX CLI is how both get work done.

tours.label: Where it came from
tours.message: The human story behind the project. The Over time tour has the full year-by-year version.

scenes.caption: ELMS:LN at Penn State, a learning network built from many small apps.
Keith Bailey championed it; Bill Rose and Bryan Ollendyke built it.
Mike Potter pointed Bryan to the web component standard.
The HAX editor came first, then HAXcms on PHP, then Node.js, the CLI and the MCP.
Now the Future Traveler works alongside everyone.

tours.label: Build a course in five minutes
tours.message: For faculty and instructional designers: a quick, use-case-driven path.

scenes.caption: Start from the course skeleton.
Pick a theme.
Drop in instructional blocks.
Watch how it is used from the dashboard, with Insights on the way.

tours.label: Migrate your site
tours.message: For people stuck on a legacy CMS: a clear way out.

scenes.caption: Your site lives in WordPress, Drupal, Plone, Notion or somewhere else.
The importers bring it in as a HAX site; open Importers for every platform and file type.
Pick a theme and the DDD blocks do the rest.
Or start from a skeleton and import into it.
A working HAXcms site, yours to publish anywhere.

tours.label: What's coming
tours.message: The Future Traveler is from the future. Planned parts show as ghosted tiles, each tied to its issue in the unified queue.

scenes.caption: Static export and Lit SSR move into core; HAX11ty becomes a wrapper.
A plugin architecture, from HAXiam system plugins down to site plugins.
One-time login links from the CLI.
Insights lands in the dashboard: stats computed from site content. What's New and Tips join it; open HAXcms for them.
AI inside HAX and the MCP leave pre-release.
Everything planned, at once.

meta.about: The UN Sustainable Development Goals HAX meets (7 of 17), generated from sdg-links.json. Only goals with evidence are shown: the point is how HAX meets them, not covering all 17. Each goal links to the pillars and parts of HAX it rests on and the wins that show it.

sdgs.desc: The UN's 17 Sustainable Development Goals, limited to the 7 HAX meets: 4 Quality Education, 7 Affordable and Clean Energy, 8 Decent Work and Economic Growth, 9 Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure, 10 Reduced Inequalities, 12 Responsible Consumption and Production, 17 Partnerships for the Goals. Goals 7 and 12 come from the HAX docs' Efficient pillar page; the rest rest on WORLDVIEW, the pledges and WINS.

sdg_4.desc: Education-led, accessible and open by default, and students learn by building a real product. Targets: 4.3 equal access to affordable tertiary education; 4.4 skills for employment; 4.5 equal access, including for persons with disabilities.
sdg_4.note: Rests on WORLDVIEW, the pledges and WINS.

sdg_7.desc: Less energy per page: web standards over large libraries, offline-capable PWAs, caching, and services that run only when called. Targets: 7.3 energy efficiency.
sdg_7.note: From the HAX docs (un-sdg on the Efficient pillar page).

sdg_8.desc: Students leave with real-product experience that carries into industry; small businesses run their own sites. Targets: 8.6 youth in education, employment or training; 8.3 small enterprises.
sdg_8.note: Rests on WORLDVIEW, the pledges and WINS.

sdg_9.desc: Open infrastructure others reuse on their own: hundreds of open web components and packages. Targets: 9.c access to information and communications technology; 9.5 research and technological capability.
sdg_9.note: Rests on WORLDVIEW, the pledges and WINS.

sdg_10.desc: Access for everyone, everywhere, regardless of physical ability, technical ability or device; performance treated as access. Targets: 10.2 inclusion of all, irrespective of disability.
sdg_10.note: Rests on WORLDVIEW, the pledges and WINS.

sdg_12.desc: Content outlives redesigns, so nothing is rebuilt; standards replace heavy libraries and whole layers of code. Targets: 12.2 efficient use of resources; 12.5 less waste.
sdg_12.note: From the HAX docs (un-sdg on the Efficient pillar page).

sdg_17.desc: Community is architecture: colleges, foundations, companies and students build HAX together. Targets: 17.17 multi-stakeholder partnerships.

meta.about: How HAX meets Penn State's strategic plan, generated from strategic-plans.json (a snapshot of https://strategicplan.psu.edu/engage/ read 2026-11-11). Only the objectives HAX meets are shown, each linked to the pillars, parts, UN goals and wins behind it. A&A's Strategic Plan 2030 opens from here.

psuplan.desc: Penn State's strategic plan, limited to what HAX meets: 7 objectives under 3 priorities, plus Growing (Inter)disciplinary Research Excellence, Transform Internal Operations, which HAX meets through A&A's plan or directly. Objectives HAX doesn't meet are left out. A snapshot read 2026-11-11.

pp_success.desc: Prepare students to be engaged citizens, employable, further educated, and able to drive positive change.

pp_research.desc: Use the University's scholarship to address major challenges facing the Commonwealth, the nation and the world. HAX meets this through A&A Goal 4: arts and design as research and practice.

pp_landgrant.desc: Contribute to the Commonwealth's economic development, workforce growth and overall vitality.

pp_deib.desc: An inclusive environment where all students, faculty and staff can flourish.

pp_tio.desc: The supporting element: initiatives that provide the infrastructure and support to carry out the plan's goals. The plan lists no objectives for it; HAX does more with less, and A&A Goal 1 aligns to it.

po_o1.desc: Advising, research advising, mentoring and class experiences that prepare students for their academic and professional futures. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

po_o2.desc: Co-curricular experiences that align students' passions, aptitudes and ambitions and lead them to success in school and work. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

po_o3.desc: Student, faculty and staff health and wellness, cultivated in a caring community focused on flourishing. HAX is the platform behind the Learn to Flourish Hub's public site. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

po_o6.desc: Use the University's assets and strategic partnerships to build resilient, sustainable communities for Pennsylvania. hax.psu.edu is a shared asset: the Innovation Hub's site and the LaunchBox small-business training site started there. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

po_o7.desc: Extend the academic enterprise through partnerships with business and industry, non-profits, communities and residents. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

po_o8.desc: Galvanize an engaged and effective network of advocates and investors in Penn State. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

po_o9.desc: Address institutional barriers to close student outcome gaps. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

aaplan.desc: The College of Arts and Architecture's Strategic Plan 2030 (2026–2030), limited to what HAX meets: 14 sub-objectives across its five goals. Sub-objectives HAX doesn't meet are left out. A snapshot read 2026-11-11.

ag_g1.desc: Strengthen trust, connection and belonging across people, partnerships and programs. A&A aligns it to Penn State's Transform Internal Operations.

ag_g2.desc: Enrich campus, community and civic life across Pennsylvania and beyond. A&A aligns it to Penn State's Increasing Land-Grant Impact.

ag_g3.desc: Develop skills, imagination and agency. A&A aligns it to Penn State's Enhancing Student Success.

ag_g4.desc: Advance discovery, insight, influence and impact. A&A aligns it to Penn State's Growing (Inter)disciplinary Research Excellence.

ag_g5.desc: Every student, faculty member and staff member has the support, access and opportunities to thrive. A&A aligns it to Penn State's Fostering Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging.

as_1a.desc: Reimagine shared physical spaces and systems to encourage collaboration. HAX Lab is a physical space for cross-discipline work like the Flourish Hub, student internships and collaborations. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

as_1b.desc: Build cross-disciplinary collaboration into curricula, research and creative practice. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

as_1c.desc: Use collaboration to reduce administrative burden rather than add to workloads. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

as_2b.desc: Expand artist residencies and student experiential opportunities. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

as_2c.desc: Embed human-centered design principles in courses, performances and creative practice. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

as_2d.desc: Strengthen A&A's visibility and partnerships at state, national and global levels. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

as_3a.desc: Expose students to diverse career pathways through arts- and design-integrated experiential learning. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

as_3b.desc: Build ethical AI literacy and future-ready skills into curricular and co-curricular experiences. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

as_3c.desc: Expand A&A's role in General Education so all students can explore creativity and emerging technologies. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

as_3d.desc: Develop new degrees, minors, certificates and hybrid learning models that match demand and workforce needs. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

as_4a.desc: Build cross-campus partnerships that raise the visibility and impact of arts and design. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

as_4b.desc: Elevate recognition of A&A's creative activity, research and scholarship. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

as_4c.desc: Lead University-wide human-centered use of AI in creative practice and research. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)

as_5b.desc: Reduce or remove affordability and access barriers to participation. (Paraphrased; see the plan for its words.)
